The validation metric is multiclass log loss.

title: draft - 00b6fe0a
description: I merged the three pipeline steps into a single, cohesive script: Step 1 handles data loading, stratified splitting, and feature engineering (extracting stylometric statistics, character/word n-grams, and POS patterns); Step 2 defines the DeBERTa-v3-large model architecture with Focal Loss and AdamW optimizer; Step 3 implements a simpler, more robust Sentence-BERT approach using frozen `all-mpnet-base-v2` embeddings with an MLP classifier, which avoids the complex bugs from prior DeBERTa fine-tuning attempts. The code loads the preprocessed texts from Step 1 (saved to disk), extracts sentence embeddings, trains the MLP classifier with label smoothing and early stopping, then generates the required submission file.
method: The code loads the Kaggle 'Spooky Author Identification' dataset (train/test CSV), maps author names to integer labels, and performs a stratified 80/10/10 split. It engineers (1) 18 sentence-level statistical features (punctuation frequencies, capitalization ratios, function-word density, etc.), (2) character TF-IDF n-grams (2-5), (3) word TF-IDF n-grams (1-3), and (4) POS tag count n-grams (2-4) via a suffix-based heuristic tagger — all combined into a sparse matrix (~35k features). It also extracts frozen 768-dim sentence embeddings using SentenceTransformer's all-mpnet-base-v2 model. A 3-layer MLP (768→256→128→3) with ReLU, dropout (0.2), Xavier init, label smoothing (0.1) and Adam (lr=2e-5, weight_decay=1e-4) is trained for up to 60 epochs with early stopping (patience 7) on validation log-loss. The best model is used to generate test predictions and a submission CSV.

title: debug - eaf80bde
description:
Looking at the error trace, I can see the exact issue:

- The model's `forward` method concatenates SBERT (384-dim) with projected TF-IDF (128-dim) → total 512-dim input
- But the branches are initialized with `input_dim=384`
- So when `branch(x)` is called with a 512-dim tensor, it fails trying to multiply (1024x512) by (384x256)

**Fix strategy**: The TF-IDF projection and concatenation happens in `forward()` but the branch layers are created with `input_dim=384` instead of accommodating the combined dimension. I need to either:
1. Change branch input dimension to 512 (combined), or
2. Remove the TF-IDF concatenation from the forward pass since the branches expect 384-dim input from SBERT alone

Option 1 is better - make the branches expect the combined dimension of 512 instead of 384. This way the model can leverage both SBERT and TF-IDF features through its multiple branches.
method: Data preprocessing: Loaded text data from CSV, label-encoded author targets, stratified train/val/test split (70/15/15). Feature engineering: Extracted Sentence-BERT embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim) plus combined TF-IDF features (char_wb n-grams 2-5 and word unigrams/bigrams, both 5000 max features each) for a total of 10384 features. Model architecture: Multi-branch attention classifier with three branches (256, 128, 64 dims), attention blocks with residual connections, gating mechanism, and label smoothing cross-entropy loss. Training: AdamW optimizer with cosine warmup schedule, mixed precision (AMP), gradient clipping, 60 epochs max, batch size 1024, early stopping with patience 7. Validation metric: multiclass log loss.
